+/**
+ * Local metadata store for scheduled task origin/binding.
+ * OpenClaw gateway cron.* API doesn't support custom fields,
+ * so we persist origin/binding locally in SQLite.
+ */
+import type { Database } from 'sql.js';
+
+export interface TaskMeta {
+  taskId: string;
+  origin: string; // JSON.stringify(TaskOrigin)
+  binding: string; // JSON.stringify(ExecutionBinding)
+}
+
+export class ScheduledTaskMetaStore {
+  constructor(private db: Database) {
+    this.ensureTable();
+  }
+
+  private ensureTable(): void {
+    this.db.run(
+      'CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scheduled_task_meta (task_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, origin TEXT NOT NULL, binding TEXT NOT NULL)'
+    );
+  }
+
+  get(taskId: string): TaskMeta | null {
+    const stmt = this.db.prepare('SELECT task_id, origin, binding FROM scheduled_task_meta WHERE task_id = ?');
+    stmt.bind([taskId]);
+    if (stmt.step()) {
+      const row = stmt.getAsObject() as { task_id: string; origin: string; binding: string };
+      stmt.free();
+      return { taskId: row.task_id, origin: row.origin, binding: row.binding };
+    }
+    stmt.free();
+    return null;
+  }
+
+  set(taskId: string, origin: unknown, binding: unknown): void {
+    this.db.run(
+      'INSERT OR REPLACE INTO scheduled_task_meta (task_id, origin, binding) VALUES (?, ?, ?)',
+      [taskId, JSON.stringify(origin), JSON.stringify(binding)]
+    );
+  }
+
+  delete(taskId: string): void {
+    this.db.run('DELETE FROM scheduled_task_meta WHERE task_id = ?', [taskId]);
+  }
+
+  list(): TaskMeta[] {
+    const results: TaskMeta[] = [];
+    const stmt = this.db.prepare('SELECT task_id, origin, binding FROM scheduled_task_meta');
+    while (stmt.step()) {
+      const row = stmt.getAsObject() as { task_id: string; origin: string; binding: string };
+      results.push({ taskId: row.task_id, origin: row.origin, binding: row.binding });
+    }
+    stmt.free();
+    return results;
+  }
+}

+import { inferOriginAndBinding } from './origin';
+import type { TaskOrigin, ExecutionBinding } from './origin';
+import type { TaskPolicy, PolicyTaskModel, PolicyTaskInput, PolicyDelivery } from './policies/types';
+import type { SessionTarget, WakeMode } from './constants';
+import { BindingKind, ScheduleKind, PayloadKind, DeliveryMode, SessionTarget as ST, WakeMode as WM } from './constants';
+
+/** Minimal wire task shape for mapping (avoids importing renderer types) */
+export interface WireTask {
+  id: string;
+  name: string;
+  description: string;
+  enabled: boolean;
+  schedule: unknown;
+  sessionTarget: SessionTarget;
+  wakeMode: WakeMode;
+  payload: unknown;
+  delivery: PolicyDelivery;
+  agentId: string | null;
+  sessionKey: string | null;
+  state: unknown;
+  createdAt: string;
+  updatedAt: string;
+}
+
+export interface TaskModelMapperResult {
+  wire: WireTask;
+  origin: TaskOrigin;
+  binding: ExecutionBinding;
+}
+
+export class TaskModelMapper {
+  fromWire(
+    wire: WireTask,
+    meta?: { origin: TaskOrigin; binding: ExecutionBinding },
+  ): PolicyTaskModel {
+    const resolved = meta ?? inferOriginAndBinding(wire);
+    return {
+      ...wire,
+      origin: resolved.origin,
+      binding: resolved.binding,
+    };
+  }
+
+  toWireInput(model: PolicyTaskModel, policy: TaskPolicy): PolicyTaskInput {
+    const wireBinding = policy.toWireBinding(model.binding);
+    return {
+      name: model.name,
+      description: model.description,
+      enabled: model.enabled,
+      schedule: model.schedule,
+      sessionTarget: wireBinding.sessionTarget,
+      wakeMode: model.wakeMode,
+      payload: model.payload,
+      delivery: model.delivery,
+      agentId: model.agentId,
+      sessionKey: wireBinding.sessionKey,
+    };
+  }
+
+  createDraft(origin: TaskOrigin, defaults: Partial<PolicyTaskInput>): PolicyTaskModel {
+    const now = new Date().toISOString();
+    const defaultBinding: ExecutionBinding = { kind: BindingKind.NewSession };
+
+    return {
+      id: `draft-${Date.now()}`,
+      name: defaults.name ?? '',
+      description: defaults.description ?? '',
+      enabled: defaults.enabled ?? true,
+      schedule: defaults.schedule ?? { kind: ScheduleKind.Every, everyMs: 3600000 },
+      sessionTarget: defaults.sessionTarget ?? ST.Main,
+      wakeMode: defaults.wakeMode ?? WM.Now,
+      payload: defaults.payload ?? { kind: PayloadKind.SystemEvent, text: '' },
+      delivery: defaults.delivery ?? { mode: DeliveryMode.None },
+      agentId: defaults.agentId ?? null,
+      sessionKey: defaults.sessionKey ?? null,
+      state: {
+        nextRunAtMs: null,
+        lastRunAtMs: null,
+        lastStatus: null,
+        lastError: null,
+        lastDurationMs: null,
+        runningAtMs: null,
+        consecutiveErrors: 0,
+      },

+      updatedAt: now,

+import {
+  isManagedSessionKey,
+  parseManagedSessionKey,
+  parseChannelSessionKey,
+} from '../main/libs/openclawChannelSessionSync';
+import {
+  OriginKind,
+  BindingKind,
+  DeliveryMode,
+  DeliveryChannel,
+} from './constants';
+
+// Re-declare origin/binding types here so common/ doesn't depend on renderer/
+// These MUST be kept in sync with src/renderer/types/scheduledTask.ts
+
+export type TaskOriginKind = OriginKind;
+
+export type TaskOrigin =
+  | { kind: typeof OriginKind.Legacy }
+  | { kind: typeof OriginKind.IM; platform: string; conversationId: string }
+  | { kind: typeof OriginKind.Cowork; sessionId: string }
+  | { kind: typeof OriginKind.Manual };
+
+export type ExecutionBinding =
+  | { kind: typeof BindingKind.NewSession }
+  | { kind: typeof BindingKind.UISession; sessionId: string }
+  | { kind: typeof BindingKind.IMSession; platform: string; conversationId: string; sessionId?: string }
+  | { kind: typeof BindingKind.SessionKey; sessionKey: string };
+
+/** Minimal ScheduledTask shape needed for inference (avoids importing renderer types) */
+interface InferableTask {
+  sessionKey?: string | null;
+  delivery?: { mode?: string; channel?: string };
+  agentId?: string | null;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Infer origin and binding from a ScheduledTask's wire fields.
+ * Used for backward compatibility with tasks that have no stored metadata.
+ * Pure function — no side effects.
+ */
+export function inferOriginAndBinding(task: InferableTask): {
+  origin: TaskOrigin;
+  binding: ExecutionBinding;
+} {
+  const sk = (task.sessionKey ?? '').trim();
+
+  // 1. Managed session key: "agent:main:lobsterai:{sessionId}"
+  if (sk && isManagedSessionKey(sk)) {
+    const parsed = parseManagedSessionKey(sk);
+    if (parsed) {
+      const channel = task.delivery?.channel;
+      const isIMChannel = task.delivery?.mode === DeliveryMode.Announce
+        && typeof channel === 'string'
+        && channel.length > 0
+        && channel !== DeliveryChannel.Last;
+
+      if (isIMChannel) {
+        return {
+          origin: { kind: OriginKind.IM, platform: channel!, conversationId: '' },
+          binding: {
+            kind: BindingKind.IMSession,
+            platform: channel!,
+            conversationId: '',
+            sessionId: parsed.sessionId,
+          },
+        };
+      }
+
+      return {
+        origin: { kind: OriginKind.Cowork, sessionId: parsed.sessionId },
+        binding: { kind: BindingKind.UISession, sessionId: parsed.sessionId },
+      };
+    }
+  }
+
+  // 2. Channel session key: "agent:{agentId}:{platform}:{conversationId}"
+  if (sk) {
+    const channelInfo = parseChannelSessionKey(sk);
+    if (channelInfo) {
+      return {
+        origin: { kind: OriginKind.IM, platform: channelInfo.platform, conversationId: channelInfo.conversationId },
+        binding: {
+          kind: BindingKind.IMSession,
+          platform: channelInfo.platform,
+          conversationId: channelInfo.conversationId,
+        },
+      };
+    }
+
+    // 2b. Has sessionKey but unknown format → session_key binding
+    return {
+      origin: { kind: OriginKind.Cowork, sessionId: '' },
+      binding: { kind: BindingKind.SessionKey, sessionKey: sk },
+    };
+  }
+
+  // 3. No sessionKey → manual origin
+  return {
+    origin: { kind: OriginKind.Manual },
+    binding: { kind: BindingKind.NewSession },
+  };
+}

+import type { TaskOrigin, ExecutionBinding } from '../origin';
+import type { TaskPolicy, PolicyTaskModel, PolicyTaskInput, PolicyDelivery, WireBinding } from './types';
+import { buildManagedSessionKey } from '../../main/libs/openclawChannelSessionSync';
+import { OriginKind, BindingKind, SessionTarget, WakeMode, DeliveryMode, DeliveryChannel, RunBehavior } from '../constants';
+
+export class CoworkTaskPolicy implements TaskPolicy {
+  readonly kind = OriginKind.Cowork;
+
+  getCreateDefaults(origin: TaskOrigin): Partial<PolicyTaskInput> {
+    if (origin.kind !== OriginKind.Cowork) {
+      throw new Error('Invalid origin for CoworkTaskPolicy');
+    }
+    return {
+      sessionTarget: SessionTarget.Main,
+      wakeMode: WakeMode.Now,
+      delivery: { mode: DeliveryMode.Announce, channel: DeliveryChannel.Last },
+    };
+  }
+
+  normalizeDraft(draft: PolicyTaskModel): PolicyTaskModel {
+    return draft;
+  }
+
+  onDeliveryChanged(draft: PolicyTaskModel, newDelivery: PolicyDelivery): PolicyTaskModel {
+    // Cowork tasks: delivery change does NOT affect binding (always bound to original session)
+    return { ...draft, delivery: newDelivery };
+  }
+
+  toWireBinding(binding: ExecutionBinding): WireBinding {
+    if (binding.kind === BindingKind.UISession) {
+      return { sessionTarget: SessionTarget.Main, sessionKey: buildManagedSessionKey(binding.sessionId) };
+    }
+    if (binding.kind === BindingKind.SessionKey) {
+      return { sessionTarget: SessionTarget.Isolated, sessionKey: binding.sessionKey };
+    }
+    return { sessionTarget: SessionTarget.Main, sessionKey: null };
+  }
+
+  describeRunBehavior(task: PolicyTaskModel): string {
+    if (task.binding.kind === BindingKind.UISession) {
+      return RunBehavior.uiSession;
+    }
+    return RunBehavior.newSession;
+  }
+
+  getReadonlyFields(): string[] {
+    return ['origin'];
+  }
+}

+
+export class IMTaskPolicy implements TaskPolicy {
+  readonly kind = OriginKind.IM;
+
+  getCreateDefaults(origin: TaskOrigin): Partial<PolicyTaskInput> {
+    if (origin.kind !== OriginKind.IM) {
+      throw new Error('Invalid origin for IMTaskPolicy');
+    }
+    return {
+      sessionTarget: SessionTarget.Main,
+      wakeMode: WakeMode.Now,
+      delivery: { mode: DeliveryMode.Announce, channel: origin.platform },
+    };
+  }
+
+  normalizeDraft(draft: PolicyTaskModel): PolicyTaskModel {
+    if (draft.binding.kind === BindingKind.IMSession
+        && draft.delivery.mode === DeliveryMode.Announce
+        && draft.delivery.channel !== draft.binding.platform) {
+      return {
+        ...draft,
+        delivery: { ...draft.delivery, channel: draft.binding.platform },
+      };
+    }
+    return draft;
+  }
+
+  onDeliveryChanged(draft: PolicyTaskModel, newDelivery: PolicyDelivery): PolicyTaskModel {
+    if (newDelivery.mode === DeliveryMode.None || newDelivery.mode === DeliveryMode.Webhook) {
+      return { ...draft, delivery: newDelivery, binding: { kind: BindingKind.NewSession } };
+    }
+    if (newDelivery.mode === DeliveryMode.Announce && newDelivery.channel) {
+      return {
+        ...draft,
+        delivery: newDelivery,
+        binding: {
+          kind: BindingKind.IMSession,
+          platform: newDelivery.channel,
+          conversationId: draft.binding.kind === BindingKind.IMSession ? draft.binding.conversationId : '',
+        },
+      };
+    }
+    return { ...draft, delivery: newDelivery };
+  }
+
+  toWireBinding(binding: ExecutionBinding): WireBinding {
+    if (binding.kind === BindingKind.IMSession && binding.sessionId) {
+      return { sessionTarget: SessionTarget.Main, sessionKey: buildManagedSessionKey(binding.sessionId) };
+    }
+    return { sessionTarget: SessionTarget.Main, sessionKey: null };
+  }
+
+  describeRunBehavior(task: PolicyTaskModel): string {
+    if (task.binding.kind === BindingKind.IMSession) {
+      return RunBehavior.imSession(task.binding.platform);
+    }
+    return RunBehavior.newSession;
+  }
+
+  getReadonlyFields(): string[] {
+    return ['origin'];
+  }
+}

+export class ManualTaskPolicy implements TaskPolicy {
+  readonly kind = OriginKind.Manual;
+
+  getCreateDefaults(): Partial<PolicyTaskInput> {
+    return {
+      sessionTarget: SessionTarget.Isolated,
+      wakeMode: WakeMode.Now,
+      delivery: { mode: DeliveryMode.Announce, channel: DeliveryChannel.Last },
+    };
+  }
+
+  normalizeDraft(draft: PolicyTaskModel): PolicyTaskModel {
+    // If IM announce channel selected but binding isn't im_session, auto-link
+    if (draft.delivery.mode === DeliveryMode.Announce
+        && typeof draft.delivery.channel === 'string'
+        && draft.delivery.channel.length > 0
+        && draft.delivery.channel !== DeliveryChannel.Last
+        && draft.binding.kind !== BindingKind.IMSession) {
+      return {
+        ...draft,
+        binding: {
+          kind: BindingKind.IMSession,
+          platform: draft.delivery.channel,
+          conversationId: '',
+        },
+      };
+    }
+    // If binding is im_session but delivery is not announce, reset
+    if (draft.binding.kind === BindingKind.IMSession
+        && draft.delivery.mode !== DeliveryMode.Announce) {
+      return { ...draft, binding: { kind: BindingKind.NewSession } };
+    }
+    return draft;
+  }
+
+  onDeliveryChanged(draft: PolicyTaskModel, newDelivery: PolicyDelivery): PolicyTaskModel {
+    if (newDelivery.mode === DeliveryMode.Announce
+        && typeof newDelivery.channel === 'string'
+        && newDelivery.channel.length > 0
+        && newDelivery.channel !== DeliveryChannel.Last) {
+      return {
+        ...draft,
+        delivery: newDelivery,
+        binding: {
+          kind: BindingKind.IMSession,
+          platform: newDelivery.channel,
+          conversationId: '',
+        },
+      };
+    }
+    if (newDelivery.mode === DeliveryMode.None || newDelivery.mode === DeliveryMode.Webhook) {
+      return { ...draft, delivery: newDelivery, binding: { kind: BindingKind.NewSession } };
+    }
+    return { ...draft, delivery: newDelivery };
+  }
+
+  toWireBinding(binding: ExecutionBinding): WireBinding {
+    switch (binding.kind) {
+      case BindingKind.NewSession:
+        return { sessionTarget: SessionTarget.Main, sessionKey: null };
+      case BindingKind.UISession:
+        return { sessionTarget: SessionTarget.Main, sessionKey: buildManagedSessionKey(binding.sessionId) };
+      case BindingKind.IMSession:
+        if (binding.sessionId) {
+          return { sessionTarget: SessionTarget.Main, sessionKey: buildManagedSessionKey(binding.sessionId) };
+        }
+        return { sessionTarget: SessionTarget.Main, sessionKey: null };
+      case BindingKind.SessionKey:
+        return { sessionTarget: SessionTarget.Isolated, sessionKey: binding.sessionKey };
+    }
+  }
+
+  describeRunBehavior(task: PolicyTaskModel): string {
+    switch (task.binding.kind) {
+      case BindingKind.NewSession: return RunBehavior.newSession;
+      case BindingKind.UISession: return RunBehavior.uiSession;
+      case BindingKind.IMSession: return RunBehavior.imSession(task.binding.platform);

+  }

+  getReadonlyFields(): string[] {
+    return [];
+  }

problem_statement:
Scheduled task handling is currently inconsistent across main and renderer code because task types, origin/binding values, delivery modes, session targets, wake modes, task statuses, and IPC channel names are represented as scattered string literals. This causes type drift and incorrect behavior when scheduled tasks are created or edited from different origins such as legacy tasks, IM conversations, cowork sessions, or manual UI creation.

Introduce a shared scheduled-task domain module that exposes centralized constants and types for all string values used as discriminants or status codes. The shared constants should cover schedule kinds, payload kinds, delivery modes, delivery channel sentinels, session targets, wake modes, task origins, execution binding kinds, task statuses, IPC channels, migration keys, and run-behavior descriptions. Existing discriminated union fields such as `kind: 'at'` may remain literal in interface definitions, but all value construction and comparisons elsewhere should use the shared constants. Scheduled task types should live in the shared scheduled-task module rather than renderer-only paths, and `ScheduledTaskDelivery.mode`, `ScheduledTask.sessionTarget`, `ScheduledTask.wakeMode`, `ScheduledTaskRun.status`, and related input/status fields should use the shared constant-derived types.

Scheduled task origin and execution binding behavior should be modeled explicitly. A scheduled task can originate from `legacy`, `im`, `cowork`, or `manual`. Execution bindings should support creating a new session, binding to an existing UI session, binding to an IM session with platform and conversation id, or binding to an explicit session key. The code that creates, normalizes, saves, and runs tasks should preserve these distinctions instead of relying only on `sessionTarget` and `sessionKey`.

Add a policy abstraction for scheduled tasks with concrete policies for legacy, IM, cowork, and manual tasks. The public API should include `TaskPolicy`, `PolicyTaskModel`, `PolicyTaskInput`, `PolicyDelivery`, `WireBinding`, `LegacyTaskPolicy`, `IMTaskPolicy`, `CoworkTaskPolicy`, `ManualTaskPolicy`, `TaskPolicyRegistry`, and a default `taskPolicyRegistry` export from `src/scheduled-task/policies`. Each policy must provide creation defaults, normalize an editable draft before save, update binding when delivery settings change, convert an execution binding to the wire-format `{ sessionTarget, sessionKey }`, describe the run behavior as a user-visible string, and report which fields are read-only in the UI.

The policy registry should return the policy matching a task origin. It must support `legacy`, `im`, `cowork`, and `manual` origins, and unknown/future origin kinds should fall back to the manual policy instead of throwing.

Manual tasks should default to an isolated session, immediate wake mode, and announce delivery to the “last” channel. When a manual task’s delivery is changed to an announce delivery with a concrete IM channel, the draft should automatically use an IM-session binding for that platform with an empty conversation id. When delivery is changed to `none` or `webhook`, the binding should reset to a new-session binding. Manual task wire binding conversion should map a new session to the main session with `sessionKey: null`, a UI session to the main session with a managed session key derived from the UI session id, an IM session with a known session id to the main session with the corresponding managed session key, an IM session without a session id to the main session with `sessionKey: null`, and an explicit session-key binding to the isolated session with the original key. Manual run-behavior descriptions should be non-empty and should include the IM platform when describing an IM-session binding. Manual tasks should have no read-only fields.

Legacy tasks should preserve existing behavior by defaulting to the main session and next-heartbeat wake mode. Legacy task normalization should continue to support old announce-channel behavior: when an announce delivery targets a concrete channel and the task is otherwise using a new-session binding, it should be treated as an IM-session binding for that channel. Changing legacy delivery to `none` or `webhook` should reset the binding to a new-session binding. Legacy wire binding should run in the main session with no session key, legacy run behavior should describe a new session, and the origin field should be read-only.

IM-origin tasks should represent tasks created from an IM platform/conversation context. Their defaults and normalization should keep the task bound to the originating IM conversation, use announce delivery appropriate for that platform, and prevent user edits from breaking the origin/binding relationship. Their run behavior should mention the IM platform, and relevant origin/binding fields should be read-only.

Cowork-origin tasks should represent tasks created from an existing cowork session. They should remain bound to the originating cowork/UI session, convert that session id into the managed session key used by the runtime, describe that they run in the existing UI/cowork session, and make origin/binding fields read-only.

Also update scheduled reminder text imports to use the new shared scheduled-task location so both main and renderer code refer to the same scheduled-task definitions.

Kit selection in Cowork needs to be represented as a first-class capability reference instead of being flattened into user-visible skills. Today, when a user selects an installed Kit such as a design or GitHub expert kit, the send flow expands that Kit into its underlying Skill IDs and stores/renders those Skill IDs as if the user had selected them directly. This causes the user message bubble and persisted metadata to show multiple low-level Skill badges rather than the Kit the user actually chose, and it makes follow-up turns prone to accidentally reusing or merging previous Kit selections.

Add a structured Kit capability model shared between renderer and main process. A selected Kit should produce a stable display reference with URI format `kit://<encoded-kit-id>@lobsterai-kits`, for example `kit://design@lobsterai-kits`, and metadata describing the Kit reference. New message metadata should be able to store `kitIds`, `kitReferences`, and `resolvedKitCapabilities` separately from `skillIds`. `metadata.skillIds` must only contain Skills directly selected by the user, not Skills expanded from Kits. Runtime or prompt-building paths may still use a separate runtime Skill list made from directly selected Skills plus Kit-expanded Skills so Kit functionality does not regress.

Installed Kit records should preserve all capability groups, not only Skills. The installed record format should include `id`, `version`, `installedAt`, `skills: { skillIds: string[] } | null`, `mcpServers: unknown[]`, and `connectors: unknown[]`. Marketplace Kit fields `mcpServers` and `connectors` may be `null` or missing and should be normalized to empty arrays when stored or resolved. Existing code that reads Skill IDs from an installed Kit should read from the nested `skills.skillIds` field.

When resolving selected Kits, the resolver should accept the current turn’s selected Kit IDs and installed Kit records, return all capability groups, and de-duplicate Skill IDs while preserving first-seen order. Missing or uninstalled Kit IDs should be skipped for runtime capability resolution without preventing a display reference from being built when marketplace metadata is available. Display references should use marketplace Kit metadata when available, including the localized Kit name, and should have `kind: "kit"`, `source: "lobsterai-kits"`, and a `kit://...@lobsterai-kits` URI.

The prompt context for selected Kits should be generated as a concise XML-style capability index for the current turn. If no Kit is selected, no Kit context prompt should be produced. For a selected Kit, the prompt should include Kit identity such as `<id>design</id>` and `<name>Design</name>`, list Skills as lightweight entries like `<skill id="design-critique" name="/design-critique" />`, and include MCP servers and connectors such as `<mcpServer id="figma" name="Figma" description="Inspect design files." />` and `<connector id="github" name="GitHub" />`. The Kit context must not include marketplace `tryAsking` examples and must not inline or mention `SKILL.md` content. If marketplace Skill metadata is unavailable, the prompt should fall back to installed Skill IDs for both the Skill `id` and `name`.

Kit and Skill selection must be scoped to the current turn. Starting a session should use only the currently active selections from the input. Continuing a session should also use only the selections made in that follow-up input. If the previous turn selected Kit A and the user now selects Kit B, the new message metadata and routing/context prompts should contain only Kit B, not a union with Kit A. If the user selects no Kit on a follow-up, no new `kitIds`, `kitReferences`, resolved Kit capabilities, or selected-Kit context should be sent for that turn. If the user selects the same Kit again, it should be treated as a new explicit selection for that turn. After successful send, the draft’s active Skill/Kit selections should not be accidentally reused by the next turn.

User-visible rendering should show Kit badges for `kitReferences` alongside direct Skill badges. Kit-expanded Skills must not be shown as Skill badges on the user message. Historical messages should remain stable even if the Kit is later uninstalled or renamed by relying on persisted Kit reference metadata where present. Re-editing a message should be able to restore both direct Skill selections and Kit selections.

Markdown rendering should treat `kit://...@lobsterai-kits` links as safe internal links so they can render as inline Kit references/badges inside LobsterAI. For example, `safeUrlTransform("kit://design@lobsterai-kits")` should return the same URL and `isInternalHref("kit://design@lobsterai-kits")` should be true. Unsafe protocols must still be stripped, for example `safeUrlTransform("javascript:alert(1)")` should return an empty string.

The project’s Plonky3 dependency stack needs to be updated from the 0.5.x series to Plonky3 v0.6.0 while preserving the existing lifted STARK prover/verifier behavior.

After the update, the workspace should compile and the existing STARK tests should continue to pass. In particular, the public AIR trait surface must match the Plonky3 v0.6.0 expectations: methods such as `periodic_columns`, `preprocessed_trace`, `preprocessed_width`, and related base AIR metadata should be available from the appropriate base AIR trait implementation rather than requiring lifted AIR implementations. Constraint evaluation should also continue to expose periodic values to AIR builders, and transition constraints should use the current transition selector API.

The lifted STARK implementation must remain compatible with the updated Plonky3 APIs for DFT/LDE generation, matrix bit-reversal/layout handling, field extension packing/unpacking, polynomial evaluation, quotient commitment, FRI/PCS interactions, and batched linear combination utilities. Code that previously depended on Plonky3 0.5.x-only helper traits, modules, or method signatures should be updated to the v0.6.0 equivalents.

Verifier-side periodic polynomial out-of-domain evaluation must remain correct. Periodic polynomial coefficients are stored in ascending degree order as produced by the inverse DFT, and evaluating them at the appropriate power of the out-of-domain point should produce the same values as before.

The dependency lockfile and changelog should reflect the breaking upgrade to Plonky3 v0.6.0.

+/// Double-ended iterator over the rows of a [`RowList`].
+struct RowIter<'a, T> {
+    elems: &'a [T],
+    widths: &'a [usize],
+}
+
+impl<'a, T> Iterator for RowIter<'a, T> {
+    type Item = &'a [T];
+
+    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
+        let (&width, rest) = self.widths.split_first()?;
+        let (row, elems) = self.elems.split_at(width);
+        self.widths = rest;
+        self.elems = elems;
+        Some(row)
+    }
+
+    fn size_hint(&self) -> (usize, Option<usize>) {
+        (self.widths.len(), Some(self.widths.len()))
+    }
+}
+
+impl<T> DoubleEndedIterator for RowIter<'_, T> {
+    fn next_back(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
+        let (&width, rest) = self.widths.split_last()?;
+        let (elems, row) = self.elems.split_at(self.elems.len() - width);
+        self.widths = rest;
+        self.elems = elems;
+        Some(row)
+    }
+}

problem_statement:
Heap item kind names and debug output should consistently match the concrete heap item type names used by the runtime.

Currently some `HeapItemKind` variants use shortened or mismatched names, such as `String`, `Symbol`, `BigInt`, `WeakVec`, or mapping ordinary objects through `ObjectValue`. This inconsistency is visible in runtime/debug output and bytecode snapshot output. For example, bytecode constant tables currently print BigInt constants as `[BigInt: 1]`, but the heap item type is `BigIntValue`.

Update the runtime heap item naming so every `HeapItemKind` name matches its corresponding heap item type name. In particular, heap items for JavaScript primitive wrapper values should use names like `StringValue`, `SymbolValue`, and `BigIntValue`, weak value vectors should be named consistently with their heap item type, and `OrdinaryObject` should be represented as `OrdinaryObject` rather than `ObjectValue`.

All code that branches on heap item kinds, allocates descriptors, registers heap item descriptors, prints heap items, or serializes/debug-formats bytecode constants must use the updated names consistently. Observable output should reflect the new names; for example, bytecode snapshot constant tables should print BigInt constants as `[BigIntValue: 1]` instead of `[BigInt: 1]`.

The heap item registration API should only require the single canonical heap item kind/type name rather than maintaining separate mismatched names. The runtime should continue to build and pass CI with the renamed heap item kinds, and existing behavior should remain unchanged apart from the corrected, consistent heap item names in debug/snapshot output.

problem_statement:
The runtime should avoid repeatedly constructing identical object shapes for built-in objects that always have the same fixed set of named properties. Common built-in shapes such as those used for function objects, closure/function instances, mapped and unmapped arguments objects, iterator result objects, property descriptor objects, string wrapper objects, arrays with standard layout, and similar runtime-created objects should be cached per `Realm` and reused when creating new objects in that realm.

Object creation paths that use one of these common fixed layouts should still produce exactly the same JavaScript-visible behavior as before. Property names, property order, descriptors, prototypes, accessors, and exotic behavior must remain correct. For example, arguments objects must still expose the correct non-enumerable `length`, `@@iterator`, and `callee` properties; unmapped arguments objects must still use the throwing `%ThrowTypeError%` accessor for `callee`; mapped arguments objects must still map indexed properties through their exotic `[[DefineOwnProperty]]`; arrays must still reject out-of-range lengths with `RangeError: array length out of range`; property descriptor objects returned by descriptor conversion must still contain the expected `value`/`writable` or `get`/`set` plus `enumerable` and `configurable` properties; and string wrapper objects must still expose the correct `length`.

The cached shapes must be realm-specific, because prototypes and intrinsics are realm-specific. Creating a new `Realm` should initialize its common-shape cache after the realm’s intrinsics are available, and garbage collection must continue to trace any cached shape pointers held by the realm.

Add a fast initialization path for objects whose shape already contains the complete fixed property layout. This path should allow all named property values to be installed at once, while preserving the existing property descriptors encoded by the shape. It should only be used for freshly allocated objects whose named property storage has not yet been populated and whose shape has the expected number of fixed properties.

Update the array creation API so callers can distinguish between creating an array with the default realm array prototype, creating one with an explicit optional prototype, and creating one from a cached common shape. Existing behavior of `array_create` should be preserved, while internal callers such as the test shell’s global `arguments` array installation should be able to request the default array shape through an explicit `ArrayCreateShape::Default` mode.

The refactor should not change JavaScript semantics or test-shell behavior. problem_statement:
The launcher core API currently exposes `InstanceSelection`, an enum that mixes the instance name with whether it is a client or server. This needs to be replaced by a clearer `Instance` type that can represent the same information while preserving all existing behavior for paths, selection, launching, configuration, mods, logs, and server/client list handling.

Introduce and use `ql_core::Instance` as the public instance identifier throughout the workspace instead of `ql_core::InstanceSelection`. `Instance` should carry the instance name and an `InstanceKind`, where `InstanceKind` distinguishes `Client` and `Server` and is serializable/deserializable using snake_case values. Public APIs that previously accepted or returned `InstanceSelection` should accept or return `Instance` instead, including launch-related APIs, jarmod APIs, JSON read/save helpers, mod manager APIs, launcher state/messages, process/log maps, and test-facing types such as process exit results.

The new API should provide convenient constructors and accessors equivalent to the old behavior. `Instance::client(name)` must create a client instance, `Instance::server(name)` must create a server instance, and `Instance::new(name, kind)` must create an instance of the specified kind. `get_name()`, `is_server()`, and `get_pair()` should continue to expose the selected name and server flag. Client instances must resolve launcher-specific data under `QuantumLauncher/instances/<NAME>/` and game data under `QuantumLauncher/instances/<NAME>/.minecraft/`. Server instances must resolve both launcher-specific and game data under `QuantumLauncher/servers/<NAME>/`.

`InstanceKind` should expose whether it represents a server and should be usable anywhere the launcher needs to choose the root list directory. Client lists must come from the launcher `instances` directory and server lists from the `servers` directory. Reloading directory watchers, sidebar updates, remembered selection handling, and “selected instance no longer exists” behavior must continue to work for both clients and servers, but should track the selected item’s kind rather than assuming remembered selections are always clients.

Configuration creation should accept an `InstanceKind` rather than a raw `is_server` boolean where appropriate, while still writing the existing `is_server` field according to the kind. Persisted selected instances should restore both the selected name and selected kind, defaulting to client behavior when older configuration data does not contain a kind.

All affected code should compile with the renamed/refactored API. Existing test and integration code should be able to create client instances with `ql_core::Instance::client(name)`, call launch APIs using shared instance names, and receive process exit results containing `ql_core::Instance` rather than `ql_core::InstanceSelection`.

problem_statement:
The CAF serialization layer is being refactored so that JSON readers and writers expose the typed text-reader/text-writer interfaces through the same inspector abstraction used by binary serialization. The goal is to let generic inspection code work with concrete serializers/deserializers through `as_serializer()` and `as_deserializer()` instead of depending on direct `value`/`list` overload calls on each implementation.

As part of this refactor, `serializer` and `deserializer` must provide the generic sequence and value handling needed by derived inspectors, including support for `std::vector<bool>`. Binary serialization of `std::vector<bool>` should preserve round-trip behavior while packing boolean values compactly into bytes. A vector with eight booleans should serialize as the length plus one packed data byte, and vectors with one, eight, nine, or zero elements must deserialize back to the original values.

The base `serializer` contract should remain usable by subclasses that only implement the primitive hooks. Calls to associative-array helpers, key-value-pair helpers, and `value(std::vector<bool>)` must delegate to the virtual primitive operations and propagate failure correctly. Implementations whose primitive value hook fails must report failure for these compound helpers, while implementations whose primitive value hook succeeds should accept even-length boolean vectors and reject odd-length vectors according to the existing serializer test contract.

Keep the public serialization behavior compatible for existing binary and JSON users while moving JSON-specific internals behind the text interface PIMPL design. The target serialization and serializer tests must continue to run through the existing CMake build and CTest selection.

CrabTalk needs the daemon protocol to own management operations that are currently handled directly by the CLI, and tool-result messages must carry the tool/function name so they can be sent to providers that require it.

Tool result messages currently only store the tool call id. This causes provider conversion to produce a tool/function response with no name, which breaks Gemini because `function_response.name` must be non-empty. `wcore::Message::tool` should accept and store the tool/function name in addition to the content and `tool_call_id`, serialize/deserialize it as part of the existing message format, and the model conversion layer should preserve that value when producing the provider message.

Hub package install and uninstall should be daemon-driven streaming operations instead of CLI-side logic. The protocol should expose install and uninstall as streams of typed progress events, with `ServerMessage` carrying a `HubEvent` oneof for step progress, warnings, setup output, and completion. The CLI should display these events and no longer run the hub install/uninstall implementation itself.

The CLI should also stop directly scanning local files for daemon-owned state. Skill tab completion should query the daemon through a `ListSkills` protocol request and cache the returned names at REPL initialization. The session console should query historical sessions through a `ListConversations` protocol request instead of reading `.jsonl` session files directly. The daemon should return conversation metadata such as agent, sender, sequence, title, file path, message count, alive seconds, and a human-readable date label, sorted with most recently active conversations first.

Provider, model, and MCP configuration must be manageable through granular daemon protocol calls rather than full config replacement or direct CLI file I/O. The protocol should support listing providers with their full provider config JSON, setting one provider, deleting one provider, setting the active model, listing provider presets, listing MCPs, and writing local MCPs. `SetProvider` must validate the resulting provider set before persisting it and return the provider config as actually loaded by the daemon. `SetActiveModel` must reject unknown models with an error like `model '<name>' not found in any provider`. Deleting an unknown provider should fail with an error like `provider '<name>' not found`.

Provider presets should be shared from core configuration rather than duplicated in the CLI. The preset list should include `anthropic`, `openai`, `google`, `ollama`, `azure`, and `custom`, including provider kind, editable/default base URL information, fixed base URL information, and default model. The protocol should represent provider kinds with an enum that includes an unknown/sentinel value. Config serialization should use the canonical `kind` field for provider type, not the old `standard` alias.

The auth TUI should require a running daemon and use only daemon protocol operations to load and save providers, MCPs, and the active model. It should no longer read or write `config.toml` or `CrabTalk.toml` directly. MCP information returned through the protocol must preserve all round-trippable fields, including `command`, `args`, `env`, `url`, `auth`, `auto_restart`, and a non-empty source such as `local` for local MCPs, so saving from the auth UI does not silently lose configuration.

The first-time provider setup path used by `attach` should use the shared provider presets and write provider config compatible with the current provider model, including the `kind` field and the preset’s default model.

Update the crabllm dependencies to the version that uses the current provider kind naming, including the OpenAI-compatible provider being represented as `Openai`, and ensure CrabTalk’s provider construction and base URL normalization still work with that provider variant.
_original_problem_statement:
feat(protocol): extend daemon protocol with management operations (#116)

* fix(model): populate function name on tool-result messages

Gemini requires function_response.name to be non-empty, but tool-result
messages never carried the function name — Message::tool() only stored
the tool_call_id and the conversion layer hardcoded name to None.

* feat(protocol): route hub operations through daemon protocol

Install and uninstall become streaming operations that send typed
HubEvent progress to the CLI instead of running hub logic client-side.
The daemon handles everything: install, reload, conflict/auth warnings,
and Setup::Prompt inference. The CLI is now a thin display client.

Protocol adds HubEvent (oneof: Step, Warning, SetupOutput, Done) to
ServerMessage. Server/Client traits change install_package and
uninstall_package from request-response to streaming. The daemon spawns
the install on a separate task with an mpsc channel bridge for the sync
on_step callback.

* feat(protocol): add ListSkills message for tab completion

The CLI now queries available skill names from the daemon via the
ListSkills protocol message instead of calling resolve_manifests()
directly. Skills are fetched once at REPL init and cached in the
input widget for tab completion.

* feat(protocol): add ListConversations for session console

The CLI console now queries historical session data from the daemon via
ListConversations instead of scanning .jsonl files directly. The daemon
owns the filesystem scanning, the CLI just displays and merges with
live session data.

* feat(protocol): add provider CRUD, MCP management, and presets

Adds targeted protocol messages for provider and MCP management:

- SetProvider/DeleteProvider/SetActiveModel for granular provider CRUD
  (avoids full config replacement and its data loss)
- ListProviderPresets exposes provider templates (anthropic, openai,
  google, ollama, azure) with kind enum, base URLs, and default models
- ListMcps/SetLocalMcps for reading all MCPs and writing local ones
- ListProviders now includes full provider config JSON
- ProviderKind proto enum with From<ApiStandard> conversion
- Provider presets moved from CLI to wcore for sharing across clients

* feat(cli): migrate auth TUI to use daemon protocol

Auth TUI now loads providers and MCPs via protocol (list_providers,
list_mcps, get_config) and saves via protocol (set_provider,
delete_provider, set_active_model, set_local_mcps). All direct file
I/O removed from auth — the daemon owns config.toml and CrabTalk.toml.

Provider presets moved from CLI to wcore (PROVIDER_PRESETS) so they're
shared across clients. attach.rs updated to use wcore presets.

* fix(protocol): address PR review feedback

- ProviderKind proto enum: add UNKNOWN=0 sentinel, shift values to 1+
- list_conversations: wrap disk scan in spawn_blocking
- set_provider: validate provider set before writing to disk

* fix(protocol): address second round of review feedback

- McpInfo: use "local" source for local MCPs, not empty string
- McpInfo: add auto_restart field to prevent silent data loss on round-trip
- set_provider: return daemon-loaded config, not client input
- set_active_model: validate model exists in a provider before writing

* refactor(protocol): remove SetConfig, reorder proto field numbers

SetConfig (full config replacement) is no longer needed — granular
provider CRUD, MCP management, and SetActiveModel cover all use cases.
Keeping GetConfig for read-only status queries.

Reorder proto field numbers by category (execution, session, provider,
mcp, agent, hub, skills, services, cron, lifecycle) since the protocol
is not stable yet.

* chore(deps): bump crabllm to 0.0.11

- ProviderKind::OpenaiCompat renamed to Openai upstream
- ProviderConfig now derives Default, simplifies to_provider_def()
- standard serde alias removed (kind is the canonical field name)
- Gemini provider now resolves function_response.name from tool_call_id

* chore(cli): remove dead stream_to_terminal, wire up custom provider naming

Remove stream_to_terminal (replaced by HubSetupOutput protocol events).
Add 'n' keybinding in preset selector for custom provider names, and
auto-enter naming flow when a preset name is already taken.

problem_statement:
Refactor the `FlatVector` data access API so read-only access and mutable access are explicit.

`FlatVector::GetData<T>(Vector &)` should no longer expose a mutable `T *`. It should return a `const T *` suitable for reading vector contents. Code that intends to write into a vector must use a new API, `FlatVector::GetDataMutable<T>(Vector &)`, which returns a mutable `T *`.

This affects all C++ code that writes through a pointer obtained from `FlatVector::GetData`, including core DuckDB code, tests, and extension patches. Typical affected patterns include assigning into result vectors in scalar functions and UDFs, filling `DataChunk` columns, writing list entries, row IDs, validity-related data, enum tags, string values, aggregate state pointers, and storage/update/WAL vectors. After the change, such code should compile only when it calls `FlatVector::GetDataMutable<T>` or another explicitly mutable writer API.

Read-only callers should continue to use `FlatVector::GetData<T>` and should receive a const pointer. Existing read-only usages such as inspecting input vectors in UDFs should remain valid. Mutable usages such as:

`auto result_data = FlatVector::GetData<bool>(result); result_data[i] = ...;`

must instead use:

`auto result_data = FlatVector::GetDataMutable<bool>(result); result_data[i] = ...;`

The public API should make it clear at compile time whether a caller is reading or modifying flat vector storage, while preserving existing behavior for code that explicitly requests mutable access.
_original_problem_statement:
Make `FlatVector::GetData` return a `const` ptr, and add `FlatVector::GetDataMutable` (#21978)

This is a refactor to the `FlatVector` API that now requires users to
make it explicit when they are planning to modify the vector, instead of
just always returning a mutable pointer.

Preferably, the [new `FlatVector::Writer`
API](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/21808) would be used in these
situations - but rewriting all of the locations that
`FlatVector::GetDataMutable` is used to this is more involved / can be
done gradually.

problem_statement:
INSERT statements should be represented in the parser as a QueryNode, analogous to the existing DeleteStatement/DeleteQueryNode and UpdateStatement/UpdateQueryNode split.

Currently, INSERT-specific parse state is stored directly on InsertStatement, which prevents INSERT from fully participating in the QueryNode hierarchy and causes missing or incomplete behavior for operations that work on QueryNode objects, such as copying, equality checks, stringification, serialization/deserialization, and use as a CTE body.

Refactor the parser representation so InsertStatement is a thin SQLStatement wrapper around an InsertQueryNode. InsertQueryNode must be a QueryNode with type QueryNodeType::INSERT_QUERY_NODE and must contain the INSERT-specific fields and behavior, including the target catalog/schema/table, optional table reference, select/value source, column list, InsertColumnOrder, DEFAULT VALUES flag, CTE map, RETURNING list, and optional OnConflictInfo.

The following behavior should work through InsertQueryNode:

Parsing `INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 2, 3)` should produce an InsertStatement whose `node` is non-null, has `type == QueryNodeType::INSERT_QUERY_NODE`, and stores `table == "t"`.

`InsertStatement::ToString()` and `InsertQueryNode::ToString()` should preserve and round-trip supported INSERT forms, including column lists, RETURNING clauses, CTEs, DEFAULT VALUES, `INSERT OR REPLACE`, `INSERT BY NAME`, and `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`.

`InsertQueryNode::Copy()` must perform a deep copy, and `InsertQueryNode::Equals()` must compare all relevant INSERT fields so that two equivalent parsed INSERT statements compare equal and statements targeting different tables do not.

Binary serialization and deserialization through `BinarySerializer::Serialize(static_cast<QueryNode &>(node), stream)` and `BinaryDeserializer::Deserialize<QueryNode>(stream)` must support QueryNodeType::INSERT_QUERY_NODE and preserve the full InsertQueryNode contents. This includes INSERT statements with RETURNING and statements with conflict handling such as `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO t VALUES (1, 2)`.

OnConflictInfo must also support copying, equality, string conversion, and binary serialization/deserialization, preserving at least the conflict action, indexed columns, optional update set info, and optional condition. Conflict actions such as REPLACE, NOTHING, UPDATE, and THROW should be handled consistently.

Existing INSERT execution behavior must remain unchanged. The following SQL forms should continue to parse, bind, execute, and stringify correctly:

`INSERT INTO t VALUES (...)`

`INSERT INTO t (a, b, c) VALUES (...)`

`INSERT INTO t VALUES (...) RETURNING a, b, c`

`WITH vals AS (...) INSERT INTO t SELECT * FROM vals RETURNING a`

`INSERT INTO t DEFAULT VALUES`

`INSERT INTO t SELECT ...`

`INSERT INTO schema_name.table_name VALUES (...)`

`INSERT OR REPLACE INTO t VALUES (...)`

`INSERT INTO t BY NAME SELECT ...`

`INSERT INTO t VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`

`INSERT INTO t VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET val = excluded.val`

All consumers of parsed INSERT statements, including binding, statement simplification, expression iteration, appender usage, autocomplete parsing, and serialization, should access INSERT-specific state through the InsertQueryNode while preserving existing public behavior of InsertStatement.
_original_problem_statement:
Refactor InsertStatement as thin wrapper over InsertQueryNode

Following the pattern established by DeleteStatement/DeleteQueryNode,
this moves all INSERT-specific fields into an InsertQueryNode QueryNode
subclass. InsertStatement now holds a single unique_ptr<InsertQueryNode>.

This enables INSERT to participate in the QueryNode hierarchy (e.g. as
CTE body), adds proper serialization/deserialization for InsertQueryNode
and OnConflictInfo, and updates all consumers (parser, binder, appender,
expression iterator, autocomplete) to access fields via the node.

problem_statement:
The GX texture and EFB copy paths need to be refactored so texture format conversion is handled outside the main GX shader, while preserving correct FIFO-visible GX state behavior.

`GXSetPixelFmt(GXPixelFmt pix_fmt, GXZFmt16 z_fmt)` is currently effectively a stub and does not emit the expected BP register writes or update decoded GX state correctly. Calling `GXSetPixelFmt` must encode the selected pixel format and Z format into the PE control register, write BP register `0x43`, and update related state so that FIFO capture/decode round-trips produce the correct `g_gxState.pixelFmt`, `g_gxState.zFmt`, and `g_gxState.zCompLocBeforeTex` values. For `GX_PF_RGB565_Z16`, the call should also cause the gen mode state to be flushed, visible as a BP write to register `0x00`. For YUV component formats such as `GX_PF_U8`, the call must also write the component mode register `0x42`, and decoding the FIFO should preserve `g_gxState.dstAlpha == UINT32_MAX`.

The implementation should support the hardware pixel format encodings used by GX: `GX_PF_RGB8_Z24`, `GX_PF_RGBA6_Z24`, `GX_PF_RGB565_Z16`, `GX_PF_Z24`, `GX_PF_Y8`, `GX_PF_U8`, `GX_PF_V8`, and `GX_PF_YUV420`. Unsupported pixel formats should fail clearly rather than silently doing nothing.

Texture sampling should be simplified so the generated GX shader no longer contains special-case sampling and conversion logic for palette or copy-converted formats. Palette textures should be converted to a regular sampled texture when loaded via `GXLoadTexObj`, using the currently loaded TLUT for the texture’s TLUT slot. If a palette texture is loaded without a corresponding TLUT, this should be reported as an error. Copy-converted palette sources should still be handled correctly.

EFB texture copies performed by `GXCopyTex` should resolve the EFB into an appropriate render texture and perform any required texture-format conversion as a separate operation instead of relying on shader sampling conversions. Copy clears must respect the current GX update masks independently: color clears should only occur when `clear` is true and color update is enabled, alpha clears only when `clear` is true and alpha update is enabled, and depth clears only when `clear` is true and depth update is enabled. `GXSetDstAlpha` behavior must be reflected in copies by applying the configured destination alpha when alpha update is enabled. Copies to `GX_TF_RGB565`, or copies from EFB pixel formats without alpha such as `GX_PF_RGB8_Z24` and `GX_PF_RGB565_Z16`, should behave as having alpha 1.0 in the resolved texture.

Texture upload buffering should be enabled again, and runtime statistics exposed through `AuroraStats` should include a new `lastTextureUploadSize` field that records the size of the most recent texture upload.

IA4 and IA8 textures should use an RG8-backed representation with swizzling so that intensity/alpha data samples correctly through the normal texture binding path. Texture binding layouts should be simplified so sampled texture and sampler binding indices correspond directly to the GX texture map index, without additional binding slots for TLUTs in the main GX shader.

Add a runtime task for changing the default font and text size used by renderers.

Applications should be able to request a change of font defaults through a new `font::set_defaults` task. The task must allow setting both the default `Font` and default text size (`Pixels`) used by newly created and existing renderers. When this task is executed in the winit runtime, the stored renderer defaults should be updated, all existing window renderers should be recreated with the new defaults, all user interfaces should be relaid out with the recreated renderer, and affected windows should be redrawn. This should make the change visible immediately without requiring the application to restart or reopen windows.

Font-related runtime actions should be grouped under a font action namespace instead of being represented as separate top-level runtime actions. Existing font loading and listing behavior must continue to work through this namespace: loading a font still sends the result through the provided channel, and listing fonts still returns the compositor’s available font families.

Renderer configuration should distinguish renderer-specific settings from compositor/window backend settings. The default font and default text size belong to `core::renderer::Settings`, with defaults of `Font::DEFAULT` and `Pixels(16.0)`. Antialiasing and vsync belong to compositor settings. Conversions from application `core::Settings` should preserve the configured font, text size, antialiasing, and vsync values in the appropriate settings type.

The renderer construction APIs should accept the renderer settings object rather than separate `default_font` and `default_text_size` parameters. In particular, the headless renderer API should be `renderer::Headless::new(settings: renderer::Settings, backend: Option<&str>)`, and compositor renderer creation should accept `renderer::Settings` so windows can be created and recreated with the current defaults.

The testing utilities and simulator/emulator should construct headless renderers using `core::renderer::Settings` derived from `core::Settings`. They should no longer special-case `Font::DEFAULT` to `"Fira Sans"`; the configured default font should be passed through unchanged. When the `fira-sans` feature is enabled, the embedded Fira Sans font should still be registered as the sans-serif family in the graphics font system so default font resolution works correctly.

problem_statement:
The native complex scalar syntax should be represented and validated as dedicated language forms rather than as ordinary builtin identifiers.

The keywords `C`, `i`, `re`, `img`, and `C_abs` must remain reserved keywords, but they must not be treated as builtin identifier names and must not allocate builtin `SymbolId`s. In particular, `is_keyword(name)` should still be true for each of these names, while `is_builtin_identifier_name(name)` should be false and `builtin_symbol_ref(name)` should return `None`.

The complex object syntax must continue to support the intended mathematical behavior. `i` is the native imaginary unit and should verify as an element of `C`. The unary forms `re(z)`, `img(z)`, and `C_abs(z)` should be valid only when their argument is in `C`, and their result should be known to be in `R` and therefore also in `C`. For example, a file should be able to verify facts such as:

```litex
i $in C
i * i = -1

forall z C:
    re(z) $in R
    img(z) $in R
    C_abs(z) $in R
    z = re(z) + img(z) * i
    C_abs(z) = sqrt(re(z) ^ 2 + img(z) ^ 2)
    C_abs(z) >= 0

forall r R:
    re(r) = r
    img(r) = 0
    C_abs(r) = abs(r)
```

The bare names `re`, `img`, and `C_abs` should no longer behave as first-class builtin function objects. Declarations or facts that rely on them as ordinary identifiers, such as `re $in fn(z C) R`, should not be required for the native complex syntax to work. Higher-order use should instead require an explicit lambda such as `fn(z C) R {re(z)}`.

All verifier logic that traverses objects should correctly handle the native complex forms, including `i`, `re(...)`, `img(...)`, and `C_abs(...)`, in the same way it handles other expression forms for well-definedness, syntactic equality, free parameter checks, forall parameter coverage, and dependency checks.

The evaluator should reject native complex syntax consistently because native complex values are symbolic and are not supported by evaluation. Any `eval` path that encounters `i`, `re(...)`, `img(...)`, or `C_abs(...)`, including after resolving an identifier to its executable definition, should fail with:

```text
eval: native complex values are symbolic and are not supported by the evaluator
```

problem_statement:
Noctalia's launcher needs first-class support for config-driven dmenu-style providers. Users should be able to define `[shell.launcher.dmenu.entry.<id>]` tables whose command is executed through the shell, whose stdout lines become launcher candidates, and whose entries can optionally provide an exec template, prefix, label, glyph, and global-search participation flag. Output lines must split a tab-delimited subtitle from the title while preserving the raw line as the selection value.

Add a `DmenuProvider` implementation that loads command output lazily once per launcher session, enforces a timeout and output-size limit, fuzzy-filters results, caps result count, and activates a result by either running the configured exec command with `{selection}` substituted or copying the selected raw line to the clipboard when no exec command is configured. Application startup and configuration reloads must register, clear, and refresh `dmenu.` providers without disturbing built-in or plugin providers.

While adding this feature, move launcher-specific settings out of `shell.panel` into a dedicated `shell.launcher` configuration table. The schema, settings registry, session provider, launcher panel layout/style logic, and config round-trip tests should all use the new `shell.launcher` fields for categories, icons, compact mode, app grid, session search, and usage sorting, while panel placement remains under `shell.panel`.

iguana’s reflection and serialization support needs to be extended and tightened for several test-visible cases across JSON, XML, protobuf, CMake, and formatting validation.

CMake should expose a build option `ENABLE_CXX26_REFLECTION` that, when enabled with a compiler supporting GCC-style C++26 static reflection, builds and runs `_cpp26` variants of the existing tests using `-std=gnu++26 -freflection`. These test executables must be registered with CTest and must be able to find the correct runtime `libstdc++` when executed. Tests that read files from the source tree, such as `test_json_files` and `test_github_events`, should have their CTest working directory set to the repository’s `test` directory so they can locate `data/` consistently, including inside GitHub Actions containers.

The C++26 reflection path should support annotations for reflected names and skipped members. A struct annotated with `ylt::reflection::reflect26::struct_name<"...">` should use that name where the serialized format has a root/type name, such as XML. A field annotated with `ylt::reflection::reflect26::field_name<"...">` should use the annotated name for JSON, XML, YAML, and protobuf schema generation and should also accept that name on input. A field annotated with `ylt::reflection::reflect26::skip_field{}` should be excluded from the reflected member list and from serialization/deserialization. Base classes annotated with `skip_base` should be excluded from recursive member collection.

JSON reflection should also honor alias metadata supplied without the normal reflection macro. For a C++20 type that provides `get_alias_field_names(T*)` returning `std::array` of `ylt::reflection::field_alias_t`, JSON output should use those aliases and JSON input should map those alias names back to the corresponding fields. For example, a type with fields `x` and `y` and aliases `"X"` and `"Y"` should serialize to `{"X":1,"Y":2}` and deserialize from `{"Y":4,"X":3}` into `x == 3` and `y == 4`.

XML required-field validation must match exact field names. If a struct has fields `id` and `identifier`, and only `id` is marked required via `REQUIRED(type, id)` or via the C++26 annotation `[[= iguana::xml_required{}]]`, then an XML document containing only `<identifier>...</identifier>` must still be rejected as missing the required `id` field. C++26 XML name annotations must also be honored: annotated struct names should control the XML root element, annotated field names should control element names, and `xml_required` should enforce presence using the effective serialized field name.

Protobuf support should cover proto3 binary wire behavior needed for interoperability and conformance-style testing. The public API should support explicit protobuf metadata both through helper descriptors returned by `get_members_impl(T*)` and through C++26 annotations. The helper API should include `pb_members(...)`, `pb_field<&T::field, N>("name")`, `pb_bytes_field`, `pb_zigzag_field`, `pb_fixed_field`, `pb_optional_field`, `pb_timestamp_field`/`as_timestamp_field`, `pb_duration_field`/`as_duration_field`, `pb_oneof_field<&T::field, Ns...>("name")`, `pb_unknown_fields_field`, and `pb_field_ex` with combinable options such as `pb_bytes`, `pb_zigzag`, `pb_fixed`, `pb_optional`, `pb_as_timestamp`/`as_timestamp`, and `pb_as_duration`/`as_duration`. The C++26 annotation equivalents should include `[[= iguana::pb_field(N)]]`, `[[= iguana::pb_bytes]]`, `[[= iguana::pb_zigzag]]`, `[[= iguana::pb_fixed]]`, `[[= iguana::pb_optional]]`, `[[= iguana::pb_oneof<N...>]]` or `[[= iguana::oneof<N...>]]`, `[[= iguana::as_timestamp]]` or `[[= iguana::pb_as_timestamp]]`, `[[= iguana::as_duration]]` or `[[= iguana::pb_as_duration]]`, and `[[= iguana::pb_unknown_fields]]`.

Explicit protobuf field numbers must be validated according to proto3 rules: valid field numbers are in `[1, 2^29 - 1]`, excluding the reserved range `[19000, 19999]`. The default field-number assignment should remain based on member order when no explicit field number is supplied. `to_proto<T>(std::string&, "package")` should generate a proto3 schema view that reflects the selected field names, field numbers, and wire-related metadata.

The protobuf reader and writer should handle proto3 binary wire cases including varint, fixed32/fixed64, length-delimited strings and bytes, signed zigzag fields, explicit optional presence, oneof fields represented by `std::variant<std::monostate, ...>`, `google.protobuf.Timestamp` and `google.protobuf.Duration` mapped to chrono types, and unknown field preservation when a message declares a `std::string` unknown-field storage member. Repeated primitive fields should be readable from packed, unpacked, multiple packed chunks, and mixed encodings; serialization should emit packed encoding according to proto3 defaults. Unknown fields, including unknown groups, must be skipped safely without unbounded recursion, and preserved unknown wire bytes should be written back unchanged when an unknown-field storage member is present.

A protobuf conformance testee executable named `iguana_conformance` should be buildable and usable with the official `conformance_test_runner`. It should support the proto3 binary/protobuf-output subset and skip unsupported categories such as JSON, text format, proto2, and non-protobuf output rather than failing unexpectedly. CMake should allow registering this with `PROTOBUF_CONFORMANCE_RUNNER` so it can be run via CTest using `--enforce_recommended`.

The clang-format check used by CI should be reproducible with clang-format 18. Provide a script `scripts/check-clang-format.sh` that accepts an optional base ref, defaults to `HEAD`, uses `clang-format-18` and `git-clang-format-18` by default, allows overriding them through `CLANG_FORMAT` and `GIT_CLANG_FORMAT`, reports missing tools with clear errors such as `error: clang-format-18 not found; install clang-format-18 or set CLANG_FORMAT.`, and fails with the existing message `The diff you sent is not formatted correctly.` followed by the suggested diff when formatting changes are required.

+By default, protobuf field numbers follow member order. For stable schemas or
+interop with existing `.proto` files, specify field numbers explicitly. On the
+legacy/non-C++26 path, `YLT_REFL_PB` remains available:
+
+```cpp
+struct account {
+  std::string name;
+  int32_t age;
+  std::vector<std::string> emails;
+};
+
+YLT_REFL_PB(account, (name, 10), (age, 20), (emails, 9));
+```
+
+With C++26 static reflection, prefer the `[[= iguana::pb_field(N)]]`
+annotation shown below; that path reads protobuf metadata from annotations and
+does not depend on `YLT_REFL_PB`.
+
+For advanced proto3 wire semantics on the non-C++26 path, use the descriptor
+helpers. The helper form keeps normal C++ field types while attaching protobuf
+schema metadata:
+
+```cpp
+struct event_msg {
+  int32_t id{};
+  std::string payload;
+  int32_t delta{};
+  uint32_t checksum{};
+  std::chrono::system_clock::time_point created_at{};
+  std::chrono::nanoseconds timeout{};
+  std::optional<int32_t> retry_count;
+  std::variant<std::monostate, int32_t, std::string> result;
+  std::string unknown;
+};
+
+inline auto get_members_impl(event_msg*) {
+  return iguana::pb_members(
+      iguana::pb_field<&event_msg::id, 1>("id"),
+      iguana::pb_bytes_field<&event_msg::payload, 3>("payload"),
+      iguana::pb_zigzag_field<&event_msg::delta, 5>("delta"),
+      iguana::pb_optional_field<&event_msg::retry_count, 6>("retry_count"),
+      iguana::pb_fixed_field<&event_msg::checksum, 7>("checksum"),
+      iguana::as_timestamp_field<&event_msg::created_at, 8>("created_at"),
+      iguana::as_duration_field<&event_msg::timeout, 9>("timeout"),
+      iguana::pb_oneof_field<&event_msg::result, 10, 12>("result"),
+      iguana::pb_unknown_fields_field<&event_msg::unknown>("unknown"));
+}
+```
+
+Helper APIs:
+
+| Helper | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| `pb_members(...)` | Returns the protobuf descriptor tuple from `get_members_impl(T*)`. |
+| `pb_field<&T::field, N>("name")` | Sets a protobuf field number and schema name. |
+| `pb_bytes_field` | Emits `bytes`; the C++ field is `std::string` or `std::string_view`, including optional/vector forms. |
+| `pb_zigzag_field` | Emits `sint32` or `sint64`; the C++ field remains `int32_t` or `int64_t`, including optional/vector forms. |
+| `pb_fixed_field` | Emits `fixed32`, `fixed64`, `sfixed32`, or `sfixed64` for 32/64-bit integer fields, including optional/vector forms. |
+| `pb_optional_field` | Emits proto3 `optional`; the C++ field must be `std::optional<T>`. |
+| `pb_timestamp_field` / `as_timestamp_field` | Encodes `std::chrono::system_clock::time_point` as `google.protobuf.Timestamp`, including optional/vector forms. |
+| `pb_duration_field` / `as_duration_field` | Encodes `std::chrono::nanoseconds` as `google.protobuf.Duration`, including optional/vector forms. |
+| `pb_oneof_field<&T::field, Ns...>("name")` | Maps `std::variant<std::monostate, ...>` alternatives to oneof field numbers. |
+| `pb_unknown_fields_field<&T::field>()` | Preserves unknown protobuf wire bytes in a single `std::string` field. |

+| `[[= iguana::as_timestamp]]` / `[[= iguana::pb_as_timestamp]]` | Same as `as_timestamp_field` / `pb_timestamp_field`. |
+| `[[= iguana::as_duration]]` / `[[= iguana::pb_as_duration]]` | Same as `as_duration_field` / `pb_duration_field`. |
+| `[[= iguana::pb_unknown_fields]]` | Same as `pb_unknown_fields_field`. |
+
+Supported proto3 wire metadata includes custom field numbers, `bytes`,
+`sint32/sint64` zigzag encoding, fixed-width integers, explicit optional
+presence, oneof, `google.protobuf.Timestamp`, `google.protobuf.Duration`, and
+unknown field preservation. Repeated primitive fields accept packed, unpacked,
+and mixed input; writers use proto3 default packed output where applicable.
+
+Field numbers must be in `[1, 2^29 - 1]` and cannot be in protobuf's reserved
+`[19000, 19999]` range. A message can have at most one unknown-field storage
+member, and it must be a `std::string`.
+
+Generate a `.proto` view of a struct with:
+
+```cpp
+std::string schema;
+iguana::to_proto<event_msg>(schema, "demo");
+```
+
+The current conformance target covers the proto3 binary/protobuf-output
+wire-only subset. JSON mapping, text format, proto2, extensions, services, and
+custom options are outside this scope.
+
+[more detail](lang/struct_pb_intro.md) and
+[change notes](iguana_reflect26_changes.md)
